Spatial structure slows epidemics, while percolation sets the threshold.

Arma Research Institute is an independent computational biology institute in Accra investigating how local contact geometry, discrete lattice dynamics, and percolation barriers govern biological and epidemic wave propagation.

01 / Research Agenda

Divisions & Focus

Classical compartmental models assume homogeneous mixing—treating biological tissues, biofilms, and communities as well-mixed fluids. Our work replaces mean-field assumptions with explicit spatial geometry and reproducible discrete-time simulations.

DIV. 01

Computational Biology

2D Moore-neighborhood SIR cellular automata modeling local pathogen propagation, self-shading recovered shells, and peak prevalence suppression.

DIV. 02

Percolation & Scaling

Finite-size scaling across L = 50, 100, and 200 lattices to locate dynamical percolation transitions (vc ≈ 55–57%) relative to static site percolation (vc ≈ 59.3%).

P(S → I) = 1 − (1 − β)k
DIV. 03

Open Scientific Computing

Deterministic NumPy SeedSequence pipelines executed to full extinction (up to 2,500 steps), eliminating finite-horizon truncation artifacts.

03 / Empirical Benchmark

Spatial CA vs. Well-Mixed Control

L = 100, n = 60 Monte Carlo trials per barrier density, carried to full extinction.

Note: Local contact geometry lowers peak prevalence from 98.39% to 17.17% at v = 0%, and remains a small fraction of well-mixed peaks across all barrier densities.

05 / The Institute

Independent Science from Accra

Founded without external grant restrictions, Arma Research Institute publishes open-access computational models, replication datasets, and lattice simulation software for spatial epidemiology and complex systems.
